Ultraviolet light does not inactivate PTCH1 directly: it creates pyrimidine-dimer lesions that are then mis-repaired into the UV-signature mutations found in this gene. The intermediates are known, hence indirect.

nodes.description: Loss of PTCH1 or activating SMO mutations result in constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling cascade. Active SMO translocates to the primary cilium and promotes activation of GLI transcription factors (GLI1, GLI2), which drive expression of target genes promoting proliferation and survival.

nodes.description: Active Hedgehog signaling promotes GLI transcription factor processing and nuclear translocation. GLI1 and GLI2 activate transcription of target genes including PTCH1, GLI1 (positive feedback), cyclin D1, MYC, and BCL2, promoting proliferation and survival of basal cells.

nodes.description: PTCH1 (Patched 1) encodes a transmembrane receptor that normally suppresses Smoothened (SMO) in the absence of Hedgehog ligand. Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 release SMO from inhibition, resulting in constitutive Hedgehog pathway activation. PTCH1 mutations occur in approximately 70% of sporadic BCCs and are the germline cause of Gorlin syndrome.

genetic_context.description: Loss-of-function of the tumor-suppressor receptor PTCH1 (a negative regulator of Hedgehog signaling); at the gene level this is loss of function, but the net pathway-level effect is constitutive activation.

nodes.description: Smoothened (SMO) is a G-protein coupled receptor-like protein that transduces Hedgehog signal. Activating mutations in SMO, though less common than PTCH1 loss, render SMO constitutively active regardless of PTCH1 status. Some SMO mutations confer resistance to vismodegib.

genetic_context.description: Activating (gain-of-function) SMO mutation locks the positive transducer in the active state independently of PTCH1, the opposite gene-level direction to PTCH1 loss but converging on the same pathway activation.

nodes.description: Second SMO inhibitor approved for locally advanced BCC. Similar mechanism of action to vismodegib with comparable efficacy profile. May provide alternative for patients intolerant of vismodegib.

nodes.description: Chronic UV exposure is the primary risk factor for BCC development. UV signature mutations (C>T transitions at dipyrimidine sites) are found in most BCCs. Both UVA and UVB contribute to BCC risk.

nodes.description: Constitutive Hedgehog signaling drives proliferation of basal cells through GLI-mediated transcription of cell cycle regulators, leading to tumor formation. The proliferating cells maintain a basal cell phenotype with peripheral palisading characteristic of BCC histology.

Hedgehog pathway inhibitor that binds and inhibits Smoothened. FDA-approved for locally advanced or metastatic BCC. Response rates of 30-60% in advanced disease. Side effects include muscle spasms, alopecia, and dysgeusia.
